corrections.why: 36.6 m is 120 ft, the height Foster's 1916 report says an unobstructed view would need. No source gives a built height.
The Association list types this site as Crowsnest; firelookout.com describes a camp and crow's nest.
Firelookout.com gives the Rogue River National Forest. Crater is the name used on the Forest Lookouts page and in the 1916 report. Editor to choose which name to show.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com gives the Rogue River National Forest; the Forest Lookouts page and its 1916 report title use the Crater National Forest. The sources do not say when or why the name changed.

notes_for_editor: The history is from 1913-1916 newspaper and report quotes reproduced on the Forest Lookouts page; the originals were not read. The brief's 36.6 m height is the hypothetical 120-foot tower, not a built height. The brief's kind 'platform' differs from the Association's Crowsnest. Do not mix this record with the Multnomah County Palmer Peak (US 634, OR 68; Mt. Hood National Forest). The July 11, 1933 panorama entry on the Jackson page also appears in the firetower.org Multnomah record, so it is left out of the story until someone checks which tower it belongs to. No photo with a licence was found. No source describes the site today.
